paraphrase: At the end of his dance the king of dancers (Śiva) sounded his drum fourteen times, wishing to uplift Sanaka and the other perfected ones; this is the net of the Śiva-sūtras.
notes: Widely quoted verse; numbering as v. 1 assumed.

checks.note: The verse 'nṛttāvasāne naṭarājarājo nanāda ḍhakkāṃ navapañcavāram | uddhartukāmaḥ sanakādisiddhān etad vimarśe śivasūtrajālam' is numbered ||1|| where Krishnamachariar reproduces the Nandikeśvara-kāśikā (with a note that it is printed with Upamanyu's commentary in the Nirṇayasāgara Mahābhāṣya), and is quoted as Nandikeśvara's Kāśikā in the Madhyasiddhāntakaumudī edition. Verse number 1 confirmed.

paraphrase: U31 reading of the opening verse: the fourteen phoneme-sūtras are the sound of Śiva's drum at the end of his dance, given to lift up Sanaka and the perfected ones — so the grammarian's list of sounds is itself revelation for liberation.
